jobs.title: Senior Product Manager (AI Agents)
jobs.description:
About Traba

Traba is building the AI operating layer for the industrial supply chain.

We started in the workforce space because contingent labor is the biggest operational pain point our manufacturing and logistics customers face. We used it to embed ourselves inside their daily operations and create a far better customer experience through technology. Now those same customers are pulling us beyond staffing into the broader operational workflows that run their facilities. That foundation gave us proprietary data from millions of shifts and deep enterprise relationships.

But our edge is more than data. By connecting to the systems running across every facility and activating the workers already on our platform to execute against them, we are building applied AI that drives real productivity gains and transforms how the global supply chain operates at scale.

We are backed by Founders Fund, Khosla Ventures, and General Catalyst.

The Role

We are looking for an entrepreneurial and experienced Product Manager to join as a founding member of the Agents team and help us build the next layer of Traba's product, an agentic platform that synthesizes the data flowing through our marketplace and operates autonomously inside our customers' supply chain workflows. Think Claude, but for Light Industrial businesses.

You'll embed deeply in our customers' operations, design and ship production agents that understand context, reason through ambiguity, make decisions, and execute work on behalf of users. This is a true 0-to-1 product role operating at the frontier of applied AI.

You will work directly with founders, product engineers, ML teams, and early design partners to define workflows, shape product strategy, and build products while the underlying model ecosystem continues changing beneath us. The assumptions, capabilities, and constraints will evolve rapidly and the product will evolve with them.

This role reports directly to our VP of Product.

What You’ll Do

Architect and steward product strategy for Traba’s AI agent platform
Solve complex customer problems by balancing user needs, technical constraints, and evolving AI capabilities
Write detailed product requirements and partner deeply with product engineers and ML teams
Rapidly validate and prototype ideas alongside customers and design partners
Design agent systems that reason through workflows, orchestrate tools, maintain context, and execute meaningful work
Define product behavior, evaluation systems, and quality frameworks that improve reliability and performance
Use data to uncover patterns and answer key product and system questions
Evolve our AI product portfolio with a deep understanding of model capabilities and system architecture
Visualize and communicate complex concepts from system behavior and evaluations to user experiences and business impact
Socialize your work across all levels and departments while synthesizing diverse stakeholder feedback

What We’re Looking For

Real agent builder.
You have launched customer-facing AI products where the system took meaningful actions on behalf of users. We are intentionally setting a high bar here. Shipping AI features, copilots, chat interfaces, wrappers, or lightweight LLM integrations alone is not enough. You understand agents that execute workflows, orchestrate systems, use tools, maintain context, and perform work autonomously.

0-to-1 operator.
You have built products from scratch with real customers and understand the realities of finding product market fit. You have launched, rebuilt, changed direction, killed ideas, and iterated toward signals. You are comfortable creating structures where no playbook exists.

AI-native problem solver.
You move quickly in environments where models evolve constantly and assumptions regularly break. You understand that building AI products often means navigating prompt rewrites, model shifts, reliability tradeoffs, and capability cliffs.

First-principles thinker.
You spend equal time thinking about why, how, and what. You understand that strong product judgment often comes from deeply understanding systems and constraints rather than applying generic playbooks.

Customer-embedded builder.
You believe the best products are built shoulder-to-shoulder with customers. You have experience deeply embedding with early customers, understanding workflows firsthand, and rapidly shipping based on direct feedback loops. Experience with forward deployed environments or customer-embedded product development models is highly valued.

Technical depth.
You are comfortable operating alongside ML engineers and highly technical teams as peers. You can understand evaluations, reason through system tradeoffs, prototype ideas, and participate deeply in technical conversations. You do not need to be an ex-engineer, but you should have strong technical instincts and enjoy getting into the details.

Builder mentality.
Inventive and scrappy problem solver. You move quickly, embrace ambiguity, and know how to create meaningful outcomes without relying on giant teams or excessive process.

Deeply collaborative.
You work seamlessly across engineering, ML, operations, design, leadership, and customers to bring new products to life.

What You’ll Bring

5 – 7 years of experience as a Product Manager
Evidence of launching products from scratch and driving meaningful customer outcomes
Experience building AI-native products or customer-facing agent systems
Strong technical abilities with the ability to work deeply with engineering and ML teams
Ability to read evaluations, reason through system performance, and prototype ideas
Experience operating in highly ambiguous startup environments with fast iteration cycles
Deep familiarity with AI tools and hands-on experience building with modern AI systems
Desire to work at a startup and cover an exceptionally wide surface area
A strong work ethic and desire to build a category-defining company

Benefits

💰 Competitive Salary

🍽️ Dinner Provided via Grubhub & stocked kitchen for NY employees
🚍 Commuter benefit

The compensation range for this position is set between $180,000 and $210,000, reflecting our market analysis and other relevant considerations. However, exceptions may be made for candidates with qualifications that significantly differ from those outlined in the job description.We also offer a highly competitive equity package designed to ensure you share meaningfully in the long-term success and upside of the business.

The position is based onsite in New York City or San Francisco, five days per week, giving you the opportunity to collaborate closely with a high-performing team in a fast-paced, energetic environment. jobs.description:
At ASAPP, our mission is simple: deliver the best AI-powered customer experience—faster than anyone else. To achieve that, we’re guided by principles that shape how we think, build, and execute. We value customer obsession, purposeful speed, ownership, and a relentless focus on outcomes. We work in tight, skilled teams, prioritize clarity over complexity, and continuously evolve through curiosity, data, and craftsmanship.

We are a team of problem solvers who thrive in fast-paced environments, love collaborating with great talent, and approach every day like it’s Day 1. We're a globally diverse team with hubs in New York City, Mountain View, Latin America, and India—embracing both hybrid and remote work to bring the best minds together, wherever they are. If you're driven by continuous learning, rapid pivots, and the challenges of building in a high-growth startup, we’d love to talk. This is more than a job—it’s a journey.

As Chief Product Officer, you will lead ASAPP's product strategy and portfolio through the next stage of growth. You will turn differentiated AI technology into products that enterprises buy repeatedly, deploy successfully, and scale. You will decide where ASAPP invests, what we become world-class at, and how the needs of an individual customer become durable platform capability.

This is a role for a strategic product leader who is still hands-on. You will operate at the executive level with customers and company leadership, and you will go deep with your product teams, researchers, engineers, and designers on requirements, architecture, production data, customer workflows, and technical tradeoffs. You will bring enterprise AI judgment, commercial instinct, and operating rigor to build a product organization that holds a high standard.

What you'll do

Strategy and portfolio

Set product direction: Define the vision and priorities for the ASAPP portfolio. Make clear choices about where we can create durable differentiation and translate customer, market, and technology shifts into a focused roadmap.
Turn technology into products: Partner with Research, Engineering, Delivery, and Security to convert advances in AI into products that are intuitive, reliable, and commercially valuable to customers.
Productize customer needs: Work directly with customers to understand their most important problems, find the patterns that repeat across enterprises, and convert those patterns into reusable product and platform capability.

Ownership and quality

Own products end to end: Lead products from incubation and early product-market fit through production deployment, adoption, expansion, and scale. Establish clear ownership, success metrics, and accountability across the portfolio.
Deliver customer outcomes: Make sure customers can deploy ASAPP’s GenerativeAgent and reach measurable value. Hold the bar on reliability, integrations, usability, configurability, adoption, speed to value, and business results.
Decide from production data: Stay close to how products and capabilities actually behave in production. Use telemetry, customer feedback, operational data, and business metrics to find issues, improve quality, and set investment priorities.
Hold the AI quality bar: Set a high standard for AI quality, evaluation, safety, reliability, latency, and observability. Partner with technical teams on the tradeoffs between speed, quality, cost, and scale.
Focus and execute: Establish clear priorities and make the hard tradeoffs. Say no when it is warranted, concentrate teams on what matters most, and partner with Engineering to ship with urgency, stability, and technical excellence.

Organization and market

Shape how we sell and deploy: Work with Sales, Marketing, Customer Success, and Delivery to refine positioning, packaging, segmentation, and product strategy based on what customers actually buy, deploy, adopt, and expand.
Lead across functions: Build trust across Research, Engineering, GTM, Delivery, and company leadership, and align the organization around product priorities and customer outcomes.
Build the team: Recruit, develop, and retain outstanding Product and Design talent. Build an organization with strong leaders, clear accountability, and excellent judgment, while staying personally engaged in the decisions that matter.

What you'll need

Enterprise AI product experience: Significant experience building and scaling AI products that enterprise customers run in production. Strong familiarity with modern generative AI, agentic systems, and workflows powered by AI.
Technical product depth: Able to engage meaningfully with researchers and engineers on AI systems, orchestration, knowledge and retrieval, evaluation, safety, latency, reliability, data, and platform architecture. You do not need to be a researcher, but you cannot outsource technical product judgment.
Builder mentality: A record of personally building products through ambiguity, finding product-market fit, and scaling from there, rather than inheriting mature products or businesses.
Enterprise product judgment: Experience in complex B2B environments with deep integrations, many stakeholders, demanding production requirements, and deployments that run for years.
Customer and commercial instinct: Comfortable with senior enterprise customers, and able to tell the difference between what one customer asks for and what the broader market will repeatedly value, buy, and deploy.
Productization ability: Demonstrated ability to find the common pattern across customer needs and turn it into a scalable product or platform capability.
Operating rigor: Strong prioritization, metrics orientation, and accountability. Comfortable making difficult tradeoffs and focusing teams on a small number of important outcomes.
Leadership: Proven ability to attract, develop, and lead exceptional Product and Design talent while remaining personally engaged in important product decisions.
Entrepreneurial spirit: Thrives in constant change, limited structure, rapid learning, and evolving product market fit.
Relationship builder: Can build trust across Research, Engineering, Sales, Delivery, and the executive team, and bring those groups together around clear product choices.

Job Title

Vice President of Product Design  

Detailed Job Description

Job Overview

The Vice President of Product Design is responsible for leading the company's overall product design strategy, design organization, and user experience vision.

This role oversees product design, user experience, user interface, design systems, customer research, and design innovation across the company's products and services.

The VP of Product Design serves as a strategic bridge between business strategy, product management, technology, customer insights, and design, ensuring that products are intuitive, differentiated, scalable, and aligned with customer and business objectives.

The position is accountable for establishing a strong design vision, improving customer experience, accelerating product innovation, and building a world-class product design organization.

Key Responsibilities
I. Product Design Strategy

Develop and execute the company's product design strategy in alignment with corporate and product objectives.

Establish design principles, standards, processes, priorities, and long-term design roadmaps.

Translate business and customer requirements into clear product design strategies.

Ensure design is integrated into product strategy and business decision-making.

II. Product Experience and User Experience

Lead the development of intuitive, consistent, and high-quality product experiences.

Oversee user experience (UX), user interface (UI), interaction design, information architecture, and customer journey design.

Identify opportunities to improve usability, accessibility, customer satisfaction, and overall product experience.

Establish user-centered design practices throughout the product development lifecycle.

III. Design Research and Customer Insights

Develop research strategies to understand customer needs, behaviors, preferences, and pain points.

Oversee user research, usability testing, customer interviews, surveys, and other research activities.

Translate customer insights and behavioral data into actionable product and design recommendations.

Partner with Product, Marketing, Sales, and Customer Success teams to maintain a strong understanding of target customers.

IV. Product Development Collaboration

Work closely with Product Management, Engineering, Technology, Marketing, and Business teams throughout the product development process.

Ensure design requirements and user experience objectives are incorporated from product concept through launch.

Participate in product planning, prioritization, prototyping, testing, and product reviews.

About Suzy

Suzy is a teammate: an always-on partner who has a deep understanding of the business — its customers, its market, its competitive landscape — and puts that knowledge to work. Suzy is here to propel teams forward, so they walk into every decision faster, sharper, and act with real conviction.

This means our customers need to feel that shift in every interaction they have with us, not just read about it in a press release.

The Role

Suzy is looking for a Senior Level Product Manager who treats time with customers as the job, not a break from it.

This role sits at the center of the business, not off to the side of it. You will spend real time with the customers who depend on Suzy every day, translate what you hear into product decisions that matter, and make sure Sales and Product are never telling two different stories about what we can do and where we are headed. As Suzy asks its customer base to trust us with something bigger than a research tool, you will be one of the people responsible for making sure that trust is earned — and that our reputation reflects the caliber of what we are actually building.

You will also own the machinery that determines whether that trust holds up: the evaluation pipeline and quality loops behind our AI capabilities. What we serve customers is only as good as how rigorously we measure it, and Product owns that call.

This person is someone who reads the market — the shifts, the tailwinds, the gaps that have yet to be moved on — and turns that into a strong, well-argued point of view about what customers need next and how to deliver it. Say it plainly. Defend it in a room where people disagree, because you have done the work to earn the conviction, not just the opinion.

Key Responsibilities

Customer Discovery & Voice of the Customer

Run a standing cadence of customer conversations — a set number of discovery calls every week, not a burst before planning — with particular focus on our new ICP, where our assumptions are least tested.
Get in front of customers constantly — calls, QBRs, site visits, win/loss conversations — and treat that time as core product work, not a break from it.
Let that cadence drive three things, not one: what we build, how we engage customers in the product, and how we go to market.
Turn what you hear into a clear, prioritized point of view on what the product should do next, backed by data and specific customer stories, not generic feedback themes.
Build the ongoing habits — customer advisory input, structured feedback loops — that keep customer input flowing into product decisions year-round, not just at renewal time.

The Evaluation Pipeline & AI Quality

Own the evaluation pipeline and the go/no-go on changes to evals, the prompt system, and prompt chaining — everything that materially drives the quality of what we serve customers.
Define eval strategies, quality loops, and failure-mode design: what we measure, what constitutes a regression, and what has to pass before a change reaches a customer.
Decide when to trust the model and when to defer to a human, and make that boundary explicit in the product rather than implicit in the code.
Hold the line on quality when speed and rigor are in tension, and be able to explain the tradeoff to Engineering, to leadership, and to a customer.

Adoption & Retention

Move usage of our AI capabilities beyond chat and chat-built surveys, into the surfaces where customers do the rest of their work.
Own the retention curve for your area and get it where it needs to be — know which behaviors predict renewal and design deliberately toward them.
Define what success looks like for your area and hold the team to it — adoption and retention, as well as the harder-to-measure signal of whether customers are more excited about the product than they were two quarters ago.
Root the roadmap in customers' real jobs to be done, not just the feature requests sitting in the backlog, so the product solves the underlying problem instead of the surface ask.

The Product–Commercial Operating Rhythm

Build and run a formal cadence connecting the roadmap to renewals and open deals: what needs to be true by when, and what it is worth in dollars.
Sit at the connective point between Sales and Product: bring what Sales is hearing in the field into roadmap conversations, and translate the roadmap into language Sales can use with confidence in front of a customer.
Partner directly with Sales and Customer Success on renewal and expansion conversations where product credibility is the deciding factor.
Build the proof points, demos, and talk tracks that let Sales tell the product story as well as Product does.
Partner on pricing and packaging so the value the product creates is value Suzy actually captures — pricing is part of the product, not a number handed down after the fact.

Market & Landscape Sensing

Maintain a regular read on our competitive set — what they are shipping, how they are positioning, and where they are winning.
Look beyond it: study how other vertical-AI companies build their products and their businesses, and what is moving in software broadly.
Turn that read into a point of view the company can act on — where we should follow, where we should differentiate, and where the market is about to move without us.

Product Strategy & Execution

Own the roadmap and prioritization decisions for your area of the platform, balancing customer signal, business strategy, and technical feasibility.
Drive the business forward, not just the product — connect the features and metrics you own directly to what moves retention, expansion, and new business.
Partner closely with Engineering, Design, and Marketing to ship work that customers actually notice.

Evangelism & Reputation

Act as one of Suzy's most visible champions for the product — able to explain what Suzy does, why it matters, and where it is headed, to a customer, a prospect, or a new hire, with the same conviction every time.
Find where Suzy is already delivering real value for customers and make sure that story gets told — to the market, to prospects, and back to the team doing the work.
Represent Suzy in customer-facing forums, webinars, and industry conversations that call for a credible, energetic product voice in the room.

Leadership Without the Org Chart

Set the standard for what strong customer instincts look like — in prioritization debates, in customer conversations, in how the team talks about the product — and hold the people around you to it.
Build enough trust across Product, Sales, Engineering, and Customer Success that people seek out your opinion before a decision gets made, not after.

About Suzy

Suzy is a teammate: an always-on partner who has a deep understanding of the business — its customers, its market, its competitive landscape — and puts that knowledge to work. Suzy is here to propel teams forward, so they walk into every decision faster, sharper, and act with real conviction.

This means our customers need to feel that shift in every interaction they have with us, not just read about it in a press release.

The Role

Suzy is looking for a Senior Level Product Manager who treats time with customers as the job, not a break from it.

This role sits at the center of the business, not off to the side of it. You will spend real time with the customers who depend on Suzy every day, translate what you hear into product decisions that matter, and make sure Sales and Product are never telling two different stories about what we can do and where we are headed. As Suzy asks its customer base to trust us with something bigger than a research tool, you will be one of the people responsible for making sure that trust is earned — and that our reputation reflects the caliber of what we are actually building.

You will also own the machinery that determines whether that trust holds up: the evaluation pipeline and quality loops behind our AI capabilities. What we serve customers is only as good as how rigorously we measure it, and Product owns that call.

This person is someone who reads the market — the shifts, the tailwinds, the gaps that have yet to be moved on — and turns that into a strong, well-argued point of view about what customers need next and how to deliver it. Say it plainly. Defend it in a room where people disagree, because you have done the work to earn the conviction, not just the opinion.

Key Responsibilities

Customer Discovery & Voice of the Customer

Run a standing cadence of customer conversations — a set number of discovery calls every week, not a burst before planning — with particular focus on our new ICP, where our assumptions are least tested.
Get in front of customers constantly — calls, QBRs, site visits, win/loss conversations — and treat that time as core product work, not a break from it.
Let that cadence drive three things, not one: what we build, how we engage customers in the product, and how we go to market.
Turn what you hear into a clear, prioritized point of view on what the product should do next, backed by data and specific customer stories, not generic feedback themes.
Build the ongoing habits — customer advisory input, structured feedback loops — that keep customer input flowing into product decisions year-round, not just at renewal time.

The Evaluation Pipeline & AI Quality

Own the evaluation pipeline and the go/no-go on changes to evals, the prompt system, and prompt chaining — everything that materially drives the quality of what we serve customers.
Define eval strategies, quality loops, and failure-mode design: what we measure, what constitutes a regression, and what has to pass before a change reaches a customer.
Decide when to trust the model and when to defer to a human, and make that boundary explicit in the product rather than implicit in the code.
Hold the line on quality when speed and rigor are in tension, and be able to explain the tradeoff to Engineering, to leadership, and to a customer.

Adoption & Retention

Move usage of our AI capabilities beyond chat and chat-built surveys, into the surfaces where customers do the rest of their work.
Own the retention curve for your area and get it where it needs to be — know which behaviors predict renewal and design deliberately toward them.
Define what success looks like for your area and hold the team to it — adoption and retention, as well as the harder-to-measure signal of whether customers are more excited about the product than they were two quarters ago.
Root the roadmap in customers' real jobs to be done, not just the feature requests sitting in the backlog, so the product solves the underlying problem instead of the surface ask.

The Product–Commercial Operating Rhythm

Build and run a formal cadence connecting the roadmap to renewals and open deals: what needs to be true by when, and what it is worth in dollars.
Sit at the connective point between Sales and Product: bring what Sales is hearing in the field into roadmap conversations, and translate the roadmap into language Sales can use with confidence in front of a customer.
